modelingNotes: OSM: the saved outline (way/55503397, 42 m, no mapped parts) gives the plan. Its minimum rectangle is 168 x 66 m with the long axis 19.7 deg east of north; the model is authored in that frame and rotated back, every element staying inside the outline (columns at y=+-25, gerberette tips at +-28.4, escalator to y=+30.2 of the +-30.5 edge).

Researched (Wikipedia "Centre Pompidou"; Rogers/Piano/Rice project descriptions): 166 x 60 m, 42 m high, steel superstructure of 14 column lines / 13 bays (12.7 m here), Peter Rice gerberettes carrying the floor trusses, six storeys, glass facades with tie-rod X bracing, colour code blue air / green water / yellow electricity / red circulation.

Inferred from the Commons references (west piazza view abd70277): outboard columns and tie-rod X over two storeys per bay, glazed tube escalator zig-zagging up the west face with red under-truss and red landings, east face carrying vertical blue ducts, green pipes and red lift shafts. Flight lengths, hoop spacing and lift bays are schematic.

Palette (6 materials): trim = white steel, roof = grey decks/tie rods, glass = glazing, stone slot = pompidou-blue, terracotta slot = pompidou-red, metal slot = pompidou-green. The yellow electrical conduits are omitted (budget of six).
Height: columns and roof trusses stay at the mapped 42 m; the escalator tops out at 38.5 m.

assets.name: Tour Eiffel
assets.axes: X east / Y up / Z south
assets.attribution: Open Landmarks; contains © OpenStreetMap contributors, ODbL-1.0
assets.licenseScope: CC BY applies to original artistic contributions only; ODbL applies to OSM-derived spatial data. Reference photographs retain their own licenses.
modelingNotes: OSM supplies centre, north alignment and the 330 m overall height (antennas included).

Key figures from the operator (https://www.toureiffel.paris/fr/le-monument/chiffres-cle): 124.9 m square base, floors at 57 m, 115 m and 276 m. Deck slabs keep the previously exported undersides (55.5, 113.8, 275.2 m).

Leg outer edge follows a log-space spline through half-widths 62.5 m (ground), 30 m (1st floor), 15.2 m (2nd), 12.1 m (160 m), 9.7 m (197 m), 7.0 m (240 m), 4.4 m (276 m) (near-linear upper taper), read off the Commons elevation photo 00.jpg; the curve is the published exponential-like wind-moment profile, not a surveyed surface.

Each pier is a four-chord box lattice (base ~25 m square, inferred) of 4 X-braced panels to the 1st floor and 4 more to the 2nd, whose inner chords stop at the 2nd-floor girders; the upper shaft has four slim corner box columns with 15 full-width X panels (panel count from photo 00.jpg).

Decorative arches: semicircular double-plane lattice girders (centred at ground level, intrados radius 38.6 m, extrados crown 41.9 m) under a see-through lattice belt truss and an open arcaded frieze (arch ribs on posts, 50-55.3 m) under thin deck slabs; arch radius and frieze arcade count are inferred.

Glazed first-floor pavilions and second-floor gallery are simplified to continuous mullioned glass rings; the intermediate platform at ~197 m (old Edoux lift change level) is placed from photo proportions.
Summit: enclosed glazed 3rd level, open terrace, four-rib campanile with lighthouse lantern and dome, stepped antenna mast to 330 m. Antenna equipment is generic.

A dark-to-light iron gradient follows the operator’s documented three-tone painting principle, not an exact claim about its present coating: https://www.toureiffel.paris/en/the-monument/painting-eiffel-tower .
Rivets, lift cars, inclined lift rails, restaurant interiors and the nighttime sparkle installation are omitted.

assets.name: Hôtel de Ville
assets.axes: X east / Y up / Z south
assets.attribution: Open Landmarks; contains © OpenStreetMap contributors, ODbL-1.0
assets.licenseScope: CC BY applies to original artistic contributions only; ODbL applies to OSM-derived spatial data. Reference photographs retain their own licenses.
modelingNotes: Plan: orthogonal re-drawing of the saved OSM outline in a frame rotated 20 deg to its dominant edge (every facade line within ~0.5 m of OSM), keeping the two large courts and the small light court open. West facade breaks read from the OSM outline: centre body 34.8 m between the flank pavilions (u=-45.4) with 8 pier projections at 4.3 m centres (7 bays, axis w=-1.7), 6.8 m recessed portal bays (u=-44.9) and 6.9 m projecting outer blocks (u=-46.3) of the flank pavilions, recessed wings and projecting corner pavilions.

Researched (fr.wikipedia "Hôtel de ville de Paris"): main facade 143 m long, centre section 18.8 m high, corner pavilions 26.8 m, campanile 50 m. The model therefore tops out at the 50 m campanile finial instead of the 40 m OSM building height; main cornice/balustrade 17.7-18.8 m, pavilion cornices 26.5 m.

Inferred from Commons references 00-05 scaled to those heights: ground floor to 8.6 m, first-floor tall mullioned windows 9.6-14.4 m between niche statues and paired colonnettes, frieze 15.4 m; wings have three storeys under the same cornice; flank-pavilion attic 18.8-26.2 m; truncated slate pavilion roofs 26.4-36.4 m (~65 deg) with metal crests, tall chimney stacks to 38.6 m and pointed corner turrets; centre roof ridge 29.6 m; clock (r 1.25 m) at 21 m in a stone frontispiece rising to 28.4 m; campanile base 22-31.2 m, two octagonal open stages, lead dome and lantern.

Simplified: the ~146 facade statues are abstract masses on consoles in a regular rhythm (west, north and south fronts and pavilions), dormers are stone lucarnes with pediments on every wing bay, roofs of the inner ranges are a generic 56 deg slate mansard with a low top, plus the mapped glass roof of the central hall and the Salle des fêtes roof. East facade and courts use the same storey grammar with plainer windows. No sculpture replicas, textures or Mapbox geometry.

assets.name: Hôtel des Invalides
assets.axes: X east / Y up / Z south
assets.attribution: Open Landmarks; contains © OpenStreetMap contributors, ODbL-1.0
assets.licenseScope: CC BY applies to original artistic contributions only; ODbL applies to OSM-derived spatial data. Reference photographs retain their own licenses.
modelingNotes: Plan and heights from the bundle OSM parts: hospital relations 3311814 (30 m, 10 m roof), 3311815/3311813 (15 m, 5 m roof) with their 15 courtyards; Saint-Louis nave way/244945091 (35.6 m, 9.8 m roof) and aisles; dome-church base way/227662017 (28 m), corner-chapel roofs (29.9 m), podium 34.2 m, drum 34.2-46.3 m, balustrade 46.3-48.1 m, attic and dome 48.1-72 m (roof 16.8 m), lantern 72-85.6 m, spire to 100 m. The exported 100 m top is kept (published figure: 107 m to the cross). Plans simplified within 1 m.

Hospital: bays sampled at ~6 m for map-scale detail (inferred from the reviewed Commons photographs 03/05); four window storeys under the 20 m cornice of the main ranges, two under the 10 m cornice of the lower east/west ranges, mansard roofs (steep brisis ~70 deg, gentle terrasson) with a regular dormer rhythm and chimney stacks. North facade (~200 m, OSM): corner pavilions, window surrounds, trophy-crowned dormers, central frontispiece with the great portal arch and the semicircular crowning (mapped round-roof part 3325221, 20->30 m).

Cour d'honneur (102 x 63 m, OSM hole): two storeys of open arcades on all four sides; the gallery is modeled 1.8 m deep (real ~4 m) so its back-wall glazing stays within the plan-registration test tolerance. Secondary courtyards: window rows, cornices and roofs without dormers (budget).

Dome church (Hardouin-Mansart): square base with Doric lower and Corinthian upper pilaster orders, entablatures and balustrade; south frontispiece at the mapped column positions (lower Doric 2.3-13.1 m, upper Corinthian on the mapped pedestals, pediment on the mapped gable part); side pediments E/W. Drum: 12 piers at 30 deg (fitted to the mapped buttress bumps), 8 buttresses grouped in pairs and 4 plain piers, each with paired columns (24), 12 tall arched windows; balustrade with fire-pots; attic with 12 arched lucarnes and volute consoles; 12 gilded ribs (Wikipedia: twelve gilded compartments with trophies hiding small lucarnes) with trophy masses, lucarnes and garlands; lantern set diagonally with arched openings and four obelisks, gilded spirelet, globe and cross.
Sculpture (Louis XIV relief, trophies, statues) is represented by abstract masses; masonry joints omitted.

assets.name: La Canopée des Halles
assets.axes: X east / Y up / Z south
assets.attribution: Open Landmarks; contains © OpenStreetMap contributors, ODbL-1.0
assets.licenseScope: CC BY applies to original artistic contributions only; ODbL applies to OSM-derived spatial data. Reference photographs retain their own licenses.
modelingNotes: OSM (retrieved 2026-09-29): three unnamed ways form the Canopee footprint: way/630511331 (building=roof, roof:material=glass, 8,636 m2, the central band that carries the patio), way/630213860 and way/630222417 (building=retail, 3 levels, 5,795 and 3,637 m2, the north and south wings). Their union (18,067 m2, about 147 x 130 m in its minimum rectangle) is the footprint; the registry row asserts identity (Wikidata Q15977258). No height or parts are mapped, so all heights are researched, not OSM.

Researched: Wikipedia (fr) La Canopee: culminates at 14.5 m above ground, Porte Lescot 26 m wide; Fayat / Metalocus / AMC / Architizer: roof of about 2.5 ha, 6,000-7,000 t of golden-lacquered steel ribs "like bones" with a skin of ~18,000 glass shingles (14,000 m2), 17 louvre ribs spanning up to 96 m, curvilinear "leaf" form, two public buildings (Conservatoire south, cultural centre north) around a central patio.

Inferred from the Commons references (panorama 66934f32, Forum des Halles 4c99b6d9/5551baea/f42dee24, model photo d72af72a): one smooth shell that falls from the crest (14.4 m) at the rim of the central opening to a low flowing eave (6-7 m) at the outline, rising to an arched glazed gable at the east throat (Porte Lescot). The opening is an organic oval about 62 x 44 m (scaled to the band between the wings); the roof is carried on 300 radial stepped lamella strips (each 3-5 m wide here, versus ~18,000 real shingles), 25 radial ribs, 4 ring ribs and a rim beam; 34 perimeter columns and 14 rim columns. The two wings are set 2 m in under the canopy with green-tinted glass skins. All shell curvature, rib pitch and column positions are schematic readings.

Deviation: the sunken Pina Bausch patio and the underground forum levels cannot be modelled below the z=0 garden plane; the opening is a void in the plaza slab with a stone parapet. Stair/escalator cascades and signage are omitted.

Palette (6): trim slot = invalides-gold (glass shell), metal = golden steel ribs/columns/mullions, glass = curtain-wall and wing glazing, roof = wing roof slabs, stone = plaza slab/plinth/parapet, entrance = Porte Lescot frame. No window material: there are no wall openings.

modelingNotes: Plan: the saved OSM footprint (way 63178753, 35 m height tag). The model is authored in a frame along the toothed Seine facade (origin at its east end, 25.3 deg from east) and rotated back; walls sit 0.6-1.3 m inside the mapped outline so mouldings (max 0.6 m) stay registered. The OSM river-side sawtooth is simplified to a straight wall.

Researched (Wikipedia "Gare d'Orsay" / "Musee d'Orsay"): Beaux-Arts station and hotel by Victor Laloux, 1898-1900; train shed 138 m long, 40 m span; 370-room Hotel Palais d'Orsay on the west and south sides; two large station clocks.

Read from the Commons references (00-05) scaled to the mapped widths: seven big arched glazed bays at ~14.5 m spacing between two 20 m clock pavilions (clock centres ~11 m and ~134 m from the east end), frieze/statue band and cornice at ~18 m, pavilion arched pediments with clocks, steep mansard roofs with a lantern and finial (total 35 m), hotel wings of ground arcade + three storeys + mansard dormers, low slate roofs with a barrel-vaulted nave behind.

Inferred: exact heights of storeys, the plan positions of the nave (y -57..-17, x -12..-133), rear roofscape hips, chimney stacks and dormer count. Sculpture is represented by abstract masses; clock hands are a fixed decorative pose.

assets.name: Cathédrale Notre-Dame de Paris
assets.axes: X east / Y up / Z south
assets.attribution: Open Landmarks; contains © OpenStreetMap contributors, ODbL-1.0
assets.licenseScope: CC BY applies to original artistic contributions only; ODbL applies to OSM-derived spatial data. Reference photographs retain their own licenses.
modelingNotes: Plan: every volume is extruded from its OSM building part (outline v96 = bundled v93, checked 2026-09-14): westwork/Galerie des chimeres 45 m, Galerie de la Vierge terrace 25 m, towers 69 m, stair turrets 33 m, aisles/tribunes 25 m, central vessel and transept 33 m walls with 12 m roofs (45 m ridges), apse cone, crossing spire 96 m, 28 mapped flying-buttress strips, 14 pier tops at 26 m and 14 pinnacles at 30 m.

Articulation is cut from inside those plans (shallow strips re-filled with pierced screens) and full-plan cornice slabs restore each footprint, so nothing projects outside a mapped part above 26 m and 50 m.

West facade levels read from the reviewed 2013 Commons elevation scaled to the mapped 69 m towers: portals to ~17 m (Last Judgment central portal wider/taller), Gallery of Kings 18-22 m (28 niches), Galerie de la Vierge balustrade to 25 m, 9.7 m west rose centred ~29.7 m flanked by paired lancets and oculi in the tower bays, Grand Gallery arcade 37.5-44.5 m (open between the towers), belfry lancets 47.8-60.6 m, crown balustrade to 69 m.

Tower tops are flat terraces with balustrade and corner pinnacles; the mapped 73 m hidden pyramidal roofs are lowered to a 3 m lead cap and the 0.4 m2 78 m finials are omitted (not visible in references).

Flying buttresses: one arched flyer per mapped strip (width = strip width), top from 32.4 m at the clerestory to 24.2 m at the pier, elliptical intrados springing at 18.2 m; the nave flyers are drawn single-span like the choir ones (the real nave has intermediate piers, not mapped). Pier tops follow OSM (26 m gabled caps in the nave, 30 m pinnacles with gablets around the choir and chevet).

Spire (Viollet-le-Duc, rebuilt 2024): octagonal openwork stages to ~62 m, crocketed needle, cross at 96 m (OSM height); the 16 copper apostle/evangelist statues on the four roof valleys are simplified patina figures.
Transept facades: portal with gable, glazed claire-voie, ~11 m rose, steep gable with small rose, corner turrets to ~47 m on the mapped turret parts. Rose tracery is a simplified rayonnant pattern.

Inferred: chapel wall/roof heights (10.5 m mapped base, lean-to to 12.8 m), tribune roofs (21-25 m lean-to), window sizes and counts per bay (bays follow the mapped flyer positions), sacristy parts without heights kept at 8.6 m. Sculpture, gargoyles and tracery cusps are omitted.

assets.name: Palais Bourbon
assets.axes: X east / Y up / Z south
assets.attribution: Open Landmarks; contains © OpenStreetMap contributors, ODbL-1.0
assets.licenseScope: CC BY applies to original artistic contributions only; ODbL applies to OSM-derived spatial data. Reference photographs retain their own licenses.
modelingNotes: OSM: complete 81-part ensemble (IGN LiDAR HD heights): 27.4 m pediment ridge, 4.6 m podium and stair block, twelve mapped river columns (18.4 m to the entablature), four-column courtyard portico (12.4 m), two south colonnades (10.3 m), 19.4 m pyramidal pavilions on rue de l'Universite, 14.8 m mansard/gambrel wings, 20.5 m hemicycle wall arc, copper hall roofs and the glazed library cupolas. Courtyard voids are preserved.

Published facts (Wikipedia, Palais Bourbon; Assemblee nationale): Poyet river front of twelve Corinthian columns under a Cortot pediment, started 1806 to echo the Madeleine; hemicycle chamber; four-column Corinthian portico on the cour d'honneur added under Louis-Philippe; library lit by cupolas. Sculpture is abstracted to masses on the right plinths.

Reference photographs 00.jpg (river front from Pont de la Concorde) and 01.jpg (front elevation) give: 12 columns of about 9-10 diameters, five doors between the columns, plain ashlar wings with a modillion cornice and end pilasters, relief panel over each wing, four seated statues on the podium cheeks, pediment tympanum of ~15 figures, inscription frieze.

Inferred: floor heights and bay rhythm of the mansard wings (three rows of tall windows, dormers on the slate mansard), window counts, door positions on the river wall, statue heights, roof skirt inset, dome profile. Column radius 0.75 m.
Copper is applied to the metal slot for the copper-tagged hall roofs and the chamber dome; zinc/slate roofs use the roof slot.

modelingNotes: Plan: the saved OSM footprint (courtyard voids kept open) and the mapped building:part ways. Walls are extruded from the union of parts per height slice, set back 0.45 m so cornices, string courses and plinths project exactly to the OSM outline.

Heights from OSM: six main pavilions with 23.6 m walls and quadruple-saltbox slate roofs to 31.2 m (wall part + roof part merged), two rear-court pavilions 21.4 m walls + 9.4 m hipped roofs to 30.8 m, linking wings 23.1 m + 3.7 m, the cross range 20.1 m + 6.6 m mansard, courtyard wings 16 m + 6 m gables (22 m), garden clock pavilion 21.1 m with dome to 28.2 m and lantern to 31.4 m, rue de Vaugirard gate pavilion 15.6 m with a 21.5 m drum and dome to 25.7/28.8 m, chimneys to 32 m (exported total height stays 32 m).

Researched (Wikipedia "Luxembourg Palace"): Salomon de Brosse 1615-1631 for Marie de Medici after the Palazzo Pitti, rusticated Florentine-inspired garden front, garden wing rebuilt by Gisors 1835-56 copying the 17th-c. front, symmetrical garden facade of pavilions around a central domed clock pavilion (Commons refs 00-05).

Inferred from the references and OSM: four-level grammar (arched rusticated ground storey, tall piano-nobile windows with alternating triangular/segmental hoods, upper storeys, cornice), steep lower mansard slope with dormers then a shallow upper slope, iron cresting and glazed skylight on each pavilion top, paired chimneys, the four free-standing columns (OSM column ways) and segmental clock pediment of the garden pavilion, the 24 OSM column ways of the rue de Vaugirard gate pavilion, the arched gallery closing the cour d'honneur.

Garden-front wings between the pavilions: OSM only gives 16.2 m walls and a raised 23 m strip behind; here they get a steep front slope to 21.6 m and a flat top up to the 23 m wall. The Senate hemicycle is a half-cone behind. Sculpture, the Medici fountain side and the western lot (outline only) are not modelled; the west lot is a low slab.

assets.name: Panthéon
assets.axes: X east / Y up / Z south
assets.attribution: Open Landmarks; contains © OpenStreetMap contributors, ODbL-1.0
assets.licenseScope: CC BY applies to original artistic contributions only; ODbL applies to OSM-derived spatial data. Reference photographs retain their own licenses.
modelingNotes: Plan from the OSM outline (way 16407465) and its 79 building:part polygons. Axis, drum centre and portico rows are fitted to the mapped columns: nave axis bearing 108 deg, drum centre = least-squares circle through the 30 mapped drum columns (r = 16.05 m, 11.25 deg spacing -> 32 columns, the documented count).

Heights from the mapped IGN LiDAR HD tags: body cornice 25.4 m, balustrade strips 26.6 m, arm roofs 26.4-32.4 m, crossing base 35 m, stylobate 35-37 m, peristyle 37-48 m, terrace balustrade 52 m, dome top 74.5 m, cross 90 m (kept as exported; published figures quote ~83 m above the Place du Pantheon).

Portico: published 22 Corinthian columns, 2 m diameter, ~20 m high, on an 11-step stair (1.8 m mapped). OSM maps 16 free columns (front row of 6, second row of 6 without the two centre ones, 4 outer columns in the third row) and the half-round bumps of 4 engaged columns on the pronaos wall; the two missing second-row centre columns (hidden behind the front row) are inferred to reach 22. Rows are moved 0-1.1 m back so the steps fit inside the outline.

Pediment 41.9 m wide rising 24.6 -> 31.0 m (mapped ridge; slope checked against the reviewed front photograph) with a recessed tympanum and simplified figure masses; inscription AUX GRANDS HOMMES LA PATRIE RECONNAISSANTE as bronze letter blocks on the frieze.

Side walls are blank (38 of 42 windows were walled up in 1791): plinth, entablature with a garland frieze, attic band and balustrade; transept/chevet fronts carry the mapped low pediments (29.9/28.4 m).

Drum: 32-column peristyle, drum wall with 16 arched windows, entablature and balustrade at 50.2-51.9 m, attic with 16 windows and pilasters, 16-rib ovoid lead dome (spring 60.4 m, r 13 m) and a 12-column lantern with cupola, ball and cross. Attic/dome split inferred from the reviewed Commons photographs (dome rise ~1.1x its radius).
Sculpture, coffering, masonry joints and the exact pronaos relief panels are simplified or omitted.

modelingNotes: The saved OSM footprint and 47 height-tagged parts define the 60 m pyramidal bell tower, 26.8 m nave/apse, low aisles, chapels and buttresses. Many chapel heights carry IGN Lidar HD provenance; original roof directions and heights are retained.

One 10.5 square metre mapped part has no height; it remains represented only by the common foundation rather than inventing a volume. Hidden internal part intersections are not a watertight building interior.

Inspected eligible references 00,03,06 confirm the tall square Romanesque tower with paired rounded bell bays, steep slate spire, long nave clerestory and attached lower street-front buildings. Bell windows, nave rhythm, stone ledges and clock are schematic map-scale inferences.

Skillion roofs include hidden stone undersides to make their volume closed and normal orientation unambiguous; no exposed sloped roofs face downward. Window and bell-bay panels use the shared light-blue window material and are clipped to actual constructed walls. Fine louvres, sculpture, clock ornament, roof crosses and individual masonry are omitted. Grey roof material substitutes for the photographed slate color.

assets.name: Église Saint-Sulpice
assets.axes: X east / Y up / Z south
assets.attribution: Open Landmarks; contains © OpenStreetMap contributors, ODbL-1.0
assets.licenseScope: CC BY applies to original artistic contributions only; ODbL applies to OSM-derived spatial data. Reference photographs retain their own licenses.
modelingNotes: Plan: the saved OSM footprint and mapped building:part ways (nave 34 m walls / 42 m roof, transept and its 37.8 m pedimented porches, aisles 17.4 m eaves, chapels, ambulatory, Lady Chapel dome 30.5 m, two towers 66.4 m and 70.3 m, twelve mapped portico columns at 6.3 m spacing on the 2.2 m platform). Built in a frame rotated 7.5 deg to the nave and rotated back so every volume stays on the OSM plan.

Researched (Wikipedia "Saint-Sulpice, Paris" and the Commons references 00-05): the west front is a double colonnade, Ionic over Roman Doric, with loggias behind; Servandoni's pediment was removed after a lightning strike in 1770 and replaced by a balustrade; the north tower was rebuilt 1777-80 (taller, neoclassical) while the south tower stayed about 5 m shorter with unfinished stonework (Wikipedia). Heights are the mapped 70.3 m and 66.4 m.

Inferred from photos: 6 front and 6 rear Doric columns (r 0.7 m) 2.2-13.2 m, Doric entablature to 15 m, Ionic columns 15-26.4 m over a balustraded loggia with five arched bays, entablature to 28.4 m and balustrade to 29.7 m; five portals and niches on the lower back wall. Towers: Doric/Ionic pilaster stages to 28.4 m, square louvred stage to 55 m, cross-pitched pedimented roof to 58.4 m, then a round belfry (octagonal core, corner colonnettes, arched louvres, balustrade, lead cap).

Nave, transept, aisles, apse and chapels: wall bays, arched windows, cornices and buttress piers are inferred from the photos and mapped part widths; the mapped 1 m skillion strips are treated as flying buttress ramps. The transept porches (colonnade under pediment) and the roof turrets beside the Lady Chapel are simplified from the mapped 37.8 m / 36 m parts.
Sculpture, reliefs, the fountain, lucarne dormers and slate coursing are omitted or abstracted; roofs use the grey roof swatch. No Mapbox geometry or textures.

modelingNotes: Plan (OSM, bundled): chapel body relation/3344874 (30 m walls), 14 buttress parts relation/3344873 (35 m with 5 m pinnacles), roof parts way/248296374 + way/248296313 (eaves 30 m, ridge 42 m, half-cone over the apse), west turrets way/248296385 + way/248296384 (36 m shafts, spirelets to 46 m), facade pinnacles relation/3344875 (31/38 m), two-storey porch relation/3344872 (15 m) with five 18 m buttress pinnacles relation/3344871, flèche way/265389509 + way/248296312 (47-75 m) with eight 52 m corner pinnacles. Total height 75 m kept.

Bays come from the mapped wall facets between buttresses: 4 nave bays per side + 7 apse bays = 15 upper windows (matches the 15 windows of the upper chapel). Nave windows get 4 lights (two pairs, two small and one large oculus), apse windows 2 lights and an oculus.

Researched dimensions (Wikipedia / Monuments nationaux): ridge ~42.5 m, spire 75 m (Lassus 1853), upper windows ~15.5 m tall, lower chapel ~6.6 m, west rose ~9 m wide (flamboyant, c.1490). Used: upper windows 10.0-25.6 m, lower chapel windows 2.6-7.2 m, floor string course 8.4 m, cornice 29.3 m, openwork balustrade 30-31.1 m, window gables (wimpergs) 26.1-31.5 m, rose Ø 7.6 m centred at 22.4 m in a pointed arch.

Inferred: porch storey levels (lower arcade to ~7 m, upper porch openings 8.2-13.4 m, terrace balustrade to 15 m, central upper gable to 17.3 m), the west gable with a small rose and crown of thorns, the lantern stage of the turrets (33-36 m), the flèche stages (openwork lancet stage 43-50.6 m, lattice needle with eight ribs, rings and a gilded fleur-de-lys crown) and the gilded ridge cresting and apse angel.

Simplified: tracery is rayonnant-schematic (no cusps), rose tracery is a flamboyant-like petal pattern, sculpture, gargoyles and crockets are omitted; the footprint pieces joining the Palais de Justice are kept as the 25 cm foundation only.

assets.licenseScope: CC BY applies to original artistic contributions only; ODbL applies to OSM-derived spatial data. Reference photographs retain their own licenses.
modelingNotes: OSM (way 16406633): the curved footprint, 59-level tag and 210 m height. No mapped building:part ways exist, so all articulation is inferred.

Researched (Wikipedia "Tour Montparnasse", Structurae): 209-210 m, 59 storeys (56 office storeys), dark smoked-glass curtain wall with vertical mullions and continuous ribbon glazing, plan of three joined arcs, technical floors and roof terrace at the top.

Model: walls are inset 0.5 m from the OSM outline so every mullion, plinth and cornice stays inside the mapped plan. 56 typical storeys of 3.59 m from a 5 m stone podium storey to 206 m; ribbon glazing per storey per wall (window material), mullions every ~1.6 m. The top two storeys (198.8-206 m) are a stepped-back louvred technical band with a cornice, roof deck, parapet, central plant core and three mast rods that end exactly at 210 m. Historic dark tint is not used (approved light palette).
Facade rhythm, technical-band height and podium treatment are visual inferences from the distant Commons references (00, 03, 05).

assets.name: Tour Saint-Jacques
assets.axes: X east / Y up / Z south
assets.attribution: Open Landmarks; contains © OpenStreetMap contributors, ODbL-1.0
assets.licenseScope: CC BY applies to original artistic contributions only; ODbL applies to OSM-derived spatial data. Reference photographs retain their own licenses.
modelingNotes: OSM (way 20326709, bundled): footprint outline (about 12 x 12 m with the buttress bulges on the west/east faces), height 52 m, building:levels 13, heritage stone. The base storey is extruded from that exact polygon; every upper storey steps back inside it (registration and total height 52 m kept).

Published facts (Wikipedia/Structurae, reviewed Commons photos 00-05): flamboyant Gothic tower built 1509-1523, about 52 m without the statue, four storeys above the ground arches; open pointed arches at ground level on all four faces; corner buttress piers with niches that step back with weathered caps; two rows of paired lancets (a short row and a tall belfry row) separated by a tracery band; central buttress on each face; blind-tracery crown under a cornice and balustrade; corner pedestals with the beasts of the evangelists; St James statue on the north-west corner pinnacle.

Inferred from photo proportions scaled to 52 m: stage breaks at 10.4, 24.1, 31.5-33, 36.6 and 48.3 m, arch size 3.6 x 8 m, bay and lancet widths. Statuary, crockets and tracery cusps are abstract masses; gargoyles are simple spouts. The Pascal statue inside the base is not modelled.
